(p-208) Sūrat al-Naṣr

Madaniyya (Medinan), and its verses are three.

﴿When the help of God comes﴾, i.e., His assistance and His granting you victory over your enemy. ﴿and the conquest﴾, i.e., the conquest of Mecca. It has been said that it refers to the genus of God's help and the absolute conquest, for the conquest of Mecca, being the key (miftah) to conquests and the point on which they depend, just as Mecca itself is the Mother of Cities (umm al-qura) and its leader, its coming was made equivalent to the coming of all other conquests and was linked to it. He, peace be upon him, was commanded to glorify and praise (God). The expression of the attainment of help and conquest by "coming" signifies that both are directed toward him, peace be upon him, and that they are on the wing of reaching him, peace be upon him, soon. It is narrated that it was revealed before the conquest, and this is the view of most (scholars). It has also been said that it was revealed during the days of tashriq at Mina in the Farewell Pilgrimage, so the word "idha" (when) in that case is considered in view of the fact that some of what falls within its scope, namely the seeing of people entering (the religion) ... etc., has not yet been completed.

The conquest of Mecca took place on the tenth days passed of the month of Ramadan in the eighth year (of the Hijra), and with the Prophet ﷺ were ten thousand of the Muhajirun and the Ansar and groups of the Arabs. He stayed there for fifteen nights. When he entered it, he stood at the door of the Ka'ba and then said: "There is no god but God alone, without partner. He fulfilled His promise, helped His servant, and defeated the confederates alone." Then he said: "O people of Mecca, what do you think I will do with you?" They said: "Good; a noble brother and the son of a noble brother." He said: "Go, for you are the freed ones (al-tulaqa')." Thus the Messenger of God ﷺ freed them, although God had enabled him to take them captive by force, and they were submissive to him; and for this reason the people of Mecca were called al-Tulaqa'. Then they pledged allegiance to him upon Islam, and then he set out toward Hawazin.

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 110, verse 2:

﴿And you see the people﴾ meaning: you see or you know them, ﴿entering into the religion of Allah﴾ meaning: the religion of Islam, the only religion that may be ascribed to Allah, the Exalted, other than which there is no religion. The clause, according to the first reading (aw "see" as perception), is a circumstantial clause (hal) relating to "the people," and according to the second reading (aw "know") it is a second object of "you see." His words, exalted is He, ﴿in multitudes﴾ are a circumstantial clause relating to the subject of "entering" (yadkhulun), meaning: they enter into it in dense groups, such as the people of Makkah, al-Ta'if, Yemen, Hawazin, and the rest of the tribes of the Arabs. Before that, they used to enter it one by one or two by two. It is related that when he, peace be upon him, conquered Makkah, the Arabs turned towards one another and said: "If he prevails over the people of the Sacred Precinct, no one will be able to withstand him." Allah, the Exalted, had already protected them from the companions of the Elephant and from everyone who intended them harm. So they entered the religion of Islam in multitudes without fighting. It has been read as "the victory of Allah and the help" (fath Allah wa al-nasr), and it has been read as "yudkhalun" in the passive voice.

**Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 110, verse 3:**

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾: say "Glory be to Allah," praising Him; or, be amazed at Allah the Exalted's facilitation of what had never occurred to anyone, that someone would overcome the people of His sacred, honoured sanctuary, and praise Him for His beautiful handiwork. This is evident according to the first narration. As for the second, perhaps he, peace be upon him, was commanded to persist in this, magnifying His blessings, not by producing amazement at what was mentioned, for that is only appropriate in the state of conquest. Or: remember Him while glorifying and praising Him, increasing in His worship and in extolling Him for the increase of His favour upon you. Or: pray to Him, praising Him for His blessings. It is narrated that when he opened the door of the Ka'bah, he prayed the forenoon prayer (Ṣalāt al-Ḍuḥā) eight rak'ahs. Or: exalt Him above what the wrongdoers say, praising Him for having fulfilled His promise. Or: extol Allah the Exalted with His attributes of majesty, praising Him for His attributes of generosity.

﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾: humbling yourself, belittling your deeds, magnifying the rights of Allah the Exalted, and making amends for what you neglected of the better course.

It is reported from ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that "he, peace be upon him, used to say much before his death: 'Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance.'"

And from him, peace be upon him: "Indeed, I seek forgiveness a hundred times in a day and a night."

It is also reported that when the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it to his Companions, they rejoiced, but al-ʿAbbas wept. He, peace be upon him, said: "What makes you weep, uncle?" He replied: "Your soul has been announced to you." He, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed it is as you say." Thereafter he was never seen laughing and joyful, peace be upon him.

It is also said that it was Ibn ʿAbbas who said this, and he, peace be upon him, said: "This youth has been given much knowledge."

Perhaps this was to indicate the completion of the matter of the call and the perfection of the affair of the religion, like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾.

It is reported that when it was revealed, "the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon and said: 'Indeed, a servant was given the choice by Allah the Exalted between this world and meeting Him, and he chose meeting Allah the Exalted.' Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, understood and said: 'We ransom you with our souls, our fathers, and our children.'"

And from him, peace be upon him, that "he called Fatimah, may Allah be pleased with her, and said: 'O my daughter, my soul has been announced to me.' She wept, and he said: 'Do not weep, for you are the first of my family to join me.'"

And from Ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, that this surah is called the Surah of Farewell. It was also said that it is a command to seek forgiveness for his Ummah.

﴿Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾ since He created the accountable people (mukallafin, those legally responsible for their acts), meaning: exceedingly accepting of their repentance. So every penitent should seek forgiveness, expecting acceptance.

From the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites the Surah of Victory is given a reward like one who witnessed with Muhammad the Conquest of Mecca."
